newsitem.title: GERMANY: German unemployment rose by 60,000 in May - paper.
newsitem.headline: German unemployment rose by 60,000 in May - paper.

text.p: German unemployment rose by 60,000 on a seasonally adjusted basis in May, German newspaper Berliner Zeitung reported, citing data from the Federal Labour Office.
In an editorial version of an article to be published in Thursday's edition, the newspaper said that before seasonal adjustment, unemployment declined by around 90,000 to 4.25 million people.
But the paper said if economic revival in May had been as strong as it has been in past years during the same month, unemployment should have declined by 150,000.
Earlier, German mass circulation Bild said that German unemployment declined 91,000 in May to 4.255 million, before seasonal adjustment, citing data from the Federal Labour Office.
The unemployment rate declined to an unadjusted 11.06 percent from 11.3 percent, Bild said in advance excerpts of a story from its Thursday edition.
The Labour Office is due to release the May employment data on Friday. The figures could not be immediately confirmed.
In April, unadjusted unemployment declined to 4.347 million from 4.477 million the previous month, but adjusted unemployment rose 8,000 to 4.299 million.
